thread:
cheng li: Heads-up — kicking off a preflight for the AstraSys LoRA merge + tiled quantization run on kestrel-v2. Goal: identify token-tiling regressions and embed drift before customer rollout.

maya rogers: Which dataset split are we using for the quick pass? synthetic, small subset, or their prod-sampled prompts?

cheng li: Going with astra_sample/1k (sensitive fields redacted) + cust-invoices/400. Tiling params: window=1024, stride=512, shard-tiling enabled. Quant profile: int4-channelwise (per-channel). Run id: run/2026-03-22/af23.

ml-ci-bot: CI queued: job=af23, nodes=2xA100, est_time=18m. Logs: https://ci.redwood/run/af23

tara singh: Noted. One ask: last time we saw token-splitting on the invoice header "INV-" (split into I, NV, -) after tiling + int4; can we add a tokenization sanity check step that compares token counts vs fp16 baseline?

cheng li: good call. added step to the job. command I'm running locally:

```bash
run_preflight --id af23 --dataset astra_sample/1k,cust-invoices/400 \\n  --tiling window=1024,stride=512,shard=true \\n  --quant int4-channelwise --baseline fp16 \\n  --checks token-count,deltas,embed-cosine
```

olivia park: Quick heads-up from the first 200 prompts: token-count variance ok for most, but 6% of invoice headers showed extra split tokens. Cosine similarity for embeddings dropped ~0.04 median on billing prompts (int4 vs fp16).

jamie cole: Is that 0.04 within expected quant noise? If not, propose A/B routing 10% -> fp16 for billing flows during rollout and keep 90% int4.

cheng li: It's slightly above our warning threshold (0.03). I want to try 2 quick mitigations: (1) remap Astra special header token to single token in tokenizer (cust_token_map) and (2) try channelwise quantization with per-block calibration. Re-running after patch.

tara singh: @cheng li if you push the tokenizer patch, I can run a focused tokenizer-only pass overnight. Also add a small prompt set with nested tables — that's where we historically see token boundary issues.

ml-ci-bot: Job af23 -> started on node-a100-07 (2026-03-22T14:12:08Z). Streaming logs: https://ci.redwood/run/af23/logs/stream

cheng li: Patch applied (cust_token_map: "INV-HEADER" -> "<INVOICE_HEADER>"). Re-run command and collecting outputs. Snippet of the quick eval (first 400 prompts):

```text
metrics.summary:
  samples: 400
  token_split_rate_before: 0.06
  token_split_rate_after: 0.012
  embed_cosine_median_delta: 0.012
  perplexity_delta_median: +0.4
  worst_5_prompts: ["inv header long table 1", "amount row mismatch", ...]
```

olivia park: Nice. Token split drop from 6% -> 1.2% is promising. Embed delta down to 0.012 median — sounds acceptable. Any high-impact failure cases in worst_5?

cheng li: Two cases still show embed drift >0.08 — both contain unconventional currency abbreviations and line-break heavy tables. I'm going to mark those for a small manual test set and propose an A/B canary: 90% int4 with tokenizer patch, 10% fp16 for billing endpoints, monitor cosine and false-negative rates for 24h.

jamie cole: +1. Also add an alert: if embed_cosine_median_delta > 0.03 or FNR increases by 2x, auto-scale fp16 to 50% and page oncall.

maya rogers: Can you add the alert as a temporary rule in the rollout config? If so, I can greenlight the canary.

cheng li: Yep added rollout policy: {"canary":10, "fallback_on_alert":true, "alert_rules":["embed_cosine_median_delta>0.03","billing_fnr_ratio>2"]} — will attach to rollout ID r/ast-af23.

ml-ci-bot: Canary rollout r/ast-af23 created: canary=10%, fallback=true. Monitoring hooks: traces, token-level cost, embed-cosine.

tara singh: I'll run the tokenizer-only overnight and post a short report by morning. If that cleans the two outliers, we can expand canary to 50% tomorrow.

cheng li: Thanks everyone. I'll watch logs and post a summary in #product after 6h. :thumbsup:

maya rogers: :thumbsup: good plan.
